"Guys, here's the statement from NFT Maker:

"Someone botted the Payment Gateway heavily, we saw millions of requests in a very short amount of time. The good news is that most requests got blocked by our Firewall.

Unfortunately though not all of these requests were blocked since the bot used a large amount of different IP addresses, so our rate-limit was not effective against that. According to our stats approximately 60% of all requests were blocked though.

That was not the main issue though. The main issue was that our hCaptcha access went down, meaning that we could not load the hcaptcha and got a big amount of error messages from the hCaptcha endpoint back. That means that our Payment Gateway loading times were either extremely slow or the Gateway didn’t load at all.

So I assume that a large portion of the NFTs did get reserved by a bot. Truth of the matter is that a bot would’ve been more effective if you simply posted the Pay-In address on Discord since then bots can very easily spam this address and get almost all NFTs.
 
Still this was an extremely bad scenario that should definitely not have happened.

So what are we doing to prevent this short-term:

- We’re further increasing the Firewall settings. This will inevitably lead to a slower user-journey and worse user experience overall but it will also prevent more bots.

- We are looking into why the Captcha went down. This should not have happened even with millions of requests. We’re also actively looking into captcha alternatives at the moment, some which might scale better and are a more secure against captcha solvers (so good bye seaplanes :/) and will make changes there in the next 12-24 hours.

Long term we’re assessing the situation and analysing the millions of logs we just collected to find good solutions to prevent this kind of behaviour. I’m personally extremely sorry for this experience and am deeply committed to winning this race against botters and people that want to screw over NFT drops." - DOT
